metadata.outputPurpose: Source-grounded design documentation for design review, conversion analysis, accessibility and SEO review, and possible future refactoring. This file does not change the landing implementation.
metadata.inspectionBasis: Generated from direct source inspection plus direct inspection of the raster assets. It is not based on visual judgment alone. Runtime-computed layout and browser-specific rendering were not measured in a live browser.

pageOverview.productBeingSold: A browser-based operating platform for dental clinics that centralizes scheduling, patients, clinical records, finance, inventory, leads, reports, notifications, fiscal organization, and management AI.
targetAudience: Clinic managers who need operational and financial visibility
Dentists who need schedules and clinical history
Reception and secretary teams managing appointments and patients
New clinics establishing their first operating system
Existing clinics migrating from paper, spreadsheets, or disconnected software
pageOverview.mainPromise: Replace fragmented tools and manual routines with one connected, secure, easy-to-use center of command for the clinic's complete patient and operational flow.

mainCta.label: Iniciar teste grátis
mainCta.offer: 7-day free trial without a credit card

overallNarrativeFlow: Establish a modern all-in-one promise and show a real dashboard in the hero.
Make the cost of paper, spreadsheets, manual confirmations, and disconnected systems explicit.
Present DentalFlow as a connected end-to-end patient journey using Flow Orbit and a six-step process.
Translate the platform into nine concrete, linked modules.
Offer visual product/brand proof through a three-slide carousel.
Build technical trust through named integrations, provider caveats, and security language.
Quantify the potential operational impact with animated estimates and a disclaimer.
Reduce switching anxiety through an assisted-migration process.
Expose three plans, annual/monthly pricing, feature availability, and risk-reduction terms.
Provide a click-to-play product overview video.
Repeat the free-trial offer in a focused final conversion block, then close with product, support, and legal navigation.
brandTone: Growth-oriented without consistently relying on aggressive sales language
pageOverview.perceivedPositioning: A vertically specialized dental clinic operating system rather than a generic CRM or appointment tool. The dark navy/cyan presentation positions it as a polished management platform, while emerald CTAs communicate action and positive outcomes.
differentiatorsFromGenericSaas: Dental-specific workflow from lead capture and scheduling through clinical records, payment, fiscal organization, and management decisions.
Explicit role context for managers, dentists, and reception staff in navigation.
A nine-module system rather than a single-feature scheduler.
Assisted migration from incumbent clinic systems.
Honest provider constraints for WhatsApp, NFS-e, AI, and payment infrastructure.
A conceptual Flow Orbit that visualizes every clinic module feeding one DentalFlow core.

typography.fontFamily: Geist Variable loaded from @fontsource-variable/geist and assigned to --font-sans/--font-heading.
typography.h1: text-4xl, sm:text-5xl, lg:text-[3.4rem], font-semibold, leading-[1.07], tracking-tight.
typography.sectionHeadings: Usually text-3xl to sm:text-4xl, font-semibold, leading-tight; carousel uses text-2xl to sm:text-3xl.
typography.eyebrows: text-xs or text-sm, font-semibold, uppercase, tracking-widest or tracking-[0.18em].
typography.body: Usually text-base or text-lg with leading-7/leading-8; supporting card copy uses text-sm leading-6.
typography.microcopy: text-xs/text-sm in slate-400 to slate-600, with emerald/cyan emphasis.

spacingRhythm.sectionPadding: Most sections use py-20 to py-24 and lg:py-24 to lg:py-32; hero uses min-h-[90svh], pt-28/32, pb-16/24.
spacingRhythm.contentWidths: max-w-5xl, max-w-6xl, or max-w-7xl with px-6 and lg:px-8.
spacingRhythm.headingToContent: Typically mt-12 to mt-14; supporting paragraph starts mt-4 or mt-5.
spacingRhythm.gridGaps: Usually gap-4 to gap-6, expanding through responsive column changes.

globalDesignSystem.cardStyle: Rounded-2xl or rounded-3xl, thin slate-200 borders on light surfaces or white/10 borders on dark surfaces, subtle background tint, restrained shadow at rest, and lift/stronger shadow on hover. Pricing cards are taller, dark, equal-height, and the recommended plan adds emerald glow and ring.
globalDesignSystem.buttonStyle: Shared Button primitive. Primary app button is dark slate; hero's main trial action uses the emerald secondary variant; dark-background secondary actions use the transparent inverse variant; final CTA uses a white override. Large CTAs are h-14 with rounded-lg and px-7. Focus rings are present, and primary hero/final buttons receive a magnetic pointer wrapper.
globalDesignSystem.iconStyle: Lucide outline icons at 16–24px, usually placed in 40–48px rounded containers. Cyan is used on dark surfaces, navy on light surfaces, emerald for positive states, amber for coming-soon, and muted slate for excluded or problem states.
globalDesignSystem.backgroundStyle: Alternating white, slate-50, and slate-950 sections. Dark sections share AuroraBackdrop's faint 60px grid and centered cyan radial glow; some dark sections disable the grid for calmer continuity.
globalDesignSystem.glassmorphismUsage: Used selectively on the fixed header, hero badge, floating appointment card, Flow Orbit labels/core, integration cards, and pricing surfaces via translucent whites, dark alpha backgrounds, border-white/10, and backdrop-blur.
globalDesignSystem.shadowsAndGlows: Light cards use shadow-sm and hover shadow-lg/xl; the hero product uses drop-shadow-2xl; Flow Orbit uses cyan radial and additive glows; integration/pricing cards use dark depth shadows; the Professional plan adds an emerald glow.
globalDesignSystem.borderAndRingPatterns: Light sections use border-slate-200; dark sections use border-white/10 or white/15. Focus-visible rings commonly use primary/40, white/40, or emerald-500. Pills use full rounding and translucent borders.
globalDesignSystem.darkLightAssumptions: PublicLayout forcibly applies the light theme, but the landing deliberately contains both dark and light authored sections. It does not adapt to user-selected dark mode; this preserves its designed marketing palette.
visualConsistencyNotes: Dark sections share a coherent navy/cyan language through AuroraBackdrop.
Rounded cards, thin borders, and Lucide icons are consistent across problems, modules, integrations, metrics, migration, pricing, and video benefits.
The carousel assets use a brighter photographic advertising style that differs materially from the code-rendered SaaS card language.
SectionDivider provides intentional animated transitions between most background changes, though the modules-to-carousel transition is a direct white-to-white continuation.

imagesAndMedia: BrandLink-owned DentalFlow logo asset; exact asset selection depends on darkMode.

copy.subheadline: Centralize agenda, pacientes, financeiro, estoque, leads, relatórios e IA em uma plataforma segura, simples e feita para a rotina real da clínica.
microcopy: Sua clínica no flow, seu crescimento é show!

interactions: Pointer-follow magnetic drift on primary CTA

responsiveBehavior.desktop: Two-column composition with unrestricted MacBook width and floating appointment card.
responsiveBehavior.mobile: Single-column layout; buttons stack; MacBook follows copy; appointment card is hidden below sm; trust text wraps.

accessibilityNotes: Single page h1 is used here.
MacBook has descriptive Portuguese alt text.

copy.eyebrow: O dia a dia sem um sistema
copy.headline: Gerir a clínica no improviso cobra um preço alto
copy.subheadline: Quando agenda, pacientes, dinheiro e estoque vivem em lugares diferentes, a operação trava — e o crescimento da clínica fica em segundo plano.
bodyTexts: Agenda em planilhas e papel — Horários remarcados na correria, encaixes esquecidos e nenhuma visão real do dia.
Confirmações feitas uma a uma — A recepção gasta horas ligando e mandando mensagem manualmente para cada paciente.
Financeiro no escuro — Entradas, saídas e inadimplência sem controle — decisões tomadas no achismo.
Prontuários espalhados — Histórico do paciente perdido entre pastas, cadernos e arquivos de difícil acesso.
Estoque controlado de memória — Materiais que acabam sem aviso e compras feitas no susto, sem previsibilidade.
Sistemas que não se conversam — Cada ferramenta de um lado, dados duplicados e retrabalho que ninguém controla.
O resultado é sempre o mesmo: retrabalho, tempo perdido e decisões no escuro. Existe um jeito melhor.

interactions: Cards are non-clickable; hover is decorative feedback only.
accessibilityNotes: Section is associated with its h2 via aria-labelledby.
Icons are decorative and aria-hidden.
Articles provide semantic card grouping.
Hover transforms are disabled under reduced motion.
sections.conversionRole: Problem-awareness and message matching. It turns common clinic frustrations into a reason to continue toward the solution.
potentialWeaknesses: The pain language is comprehensive but generic to many service businesses; only prontuários and clinic context are distinctly dental.
refactorNotes: Pain-point content is defined inline and could move to typed data if localization or reuse becomes necessary.

Mobile/touch/reduced-motion SVG and HTML fallback generated from source
Zero-layout-shift poster while lazy chunks or viewport trigger are pending

interactions: Fine-pointer movement subtly shifts the desktop camera; the visual is otherwise non-interactive and decorative.

responsiveBehavior.desktopFinePointer: Lazy-loads FlowOrbit, then only loads WebGL scene after its wrapper enters the viewport.
responsiveBehavior.mobileOrCoarsePointer: Uses the lightweight static SVG/HTML orbit; satellite text labels hide below sm while icons remain.
responsiveBehavior.reducedMotion: Uses fallback and CSS animation gates leave it fully static.
responsiveBehavior.journeyGrid: 2 columns by default, 3 at sm, 6 at lg; connector line appears only at lg.

accessibilityNotes: Entire orbit is aria-hidden because nearby text communicates the meaning.
Section heading is linked via aria-labelledby.
Journey icons are aria-hidden while labels remain text.
Reduced-motion preference is reactive and avoids WebGL entirely.
sections.conversionRole: Core explanatory centerpiece. It makes the all-in-one claim memorable and connects abstract platform breadth to a concrete patient journey.
potentialWeaknesses: The WebGL centerpiece may command more attention than the six-step explanation.
The orbit is fully decorative, so its eight-module labels are not independently exposed to assistive technology; this is acceptable only because the modules are fully repeated later.
Three nested lazy/visibility states increase implementation complexity.
refactorNotes: Desktop and fallback repeat the same eight module definitions in separate files; a shared typed constant could prevent drift.
Both SolutionSection and FlowOrbit define an OrbitPoster variant.

Pacientes — Cadastro completo, histórico de relacionamento e contato centralizado.
Prontuário eletrônico — Evoluções clínicas, modelos reutilizáveis e histórico sempre à mão.
Gestão financeira — Receitas, despesas, categorias e fluxo de caixa em tempo real.
Controle de estoque — Produtos, movimentações e reposição sem depender da memória.

buttons: Saber mais on every module card

Controle financeiro completo — Fluxo de caixa, lançamentos de entradas e saídas, e relatórios consolidados por período — tudo em um só painel.
Captação e gestão de leads — Pipeline de novos contatos, origem dos pacientes e acompanhamento de cada lead até a primeira consulta.

copy.headline: Integrações que conectam sua clínica ao fluxo ideal
copy.subheadline: Agenda, comunicação, pagamentos, IA, dados e fiscal em um só lugar — cada conexão documentada e com propósito claro.
bodyTexts: Google Calendar — A agenda do DentalFlow sincroniza com o Google Calendar. Horários, confirmações e disponibilidade ficam acessíveis fora do sistema — sem retrabalho de atualização manual. Benefício: Dentistas acompanham seus horários em qualquer dispositivo, sem precisar abrir o sistema.

Stripe — A cobrança da assinatura do DentalFlow passa pelo Stripe com integração server-side. Nenhum dado sensível de pagamento trafega pelo frontend da clínica. Benefício: Assinaturas da plataforma processadas de forma segura, sem exposição de tokens no frontend.

OpenAI — O assistente de IA do DentalFlow usa a API da OpenAI para analisar financeiro, estoque e agenda da clínica, gerando insights práticos e alertas contextualizados. Benefício: O gestor recebe análises e alertas baseados nos dados reais da operação, sem precisar interpretar planilhas.

WhatsApp Cloud API — Notificações de consulta, lembretes e confirmações via WhatsApp. Requer conta Business aprovada pela Meta e configuração de templates. Nosso suporte orienta o processo. Benefício: Lembretes e confirmações enviados automaticamente — sem ligações manuais da recepção.

Supabase — Banco de dados moderno usado para armazenar as informações da clínica com segurança, organização e escalabilidade. Cada clínica tem seus dados completamente separados das demais. Benefício: Dados de cada clínica isolados, seguros e acessíveis — sem depender de servidores próprios.

Provedor NFS-e — O módulo fiscal centraliza rascunhos de notas e vincula serviços a consultas. A emissão de NFS-e oficial via provedor homologado está em desenvolvimento. Benefício: Dados fiscais organizados internamente hoje, prontos para emissão oficial quando o provedor estiver disponível.
badges: Menos operação manual, mais fluxo centralizado
Cada integração documentada no produto ou roadmap confirmado
Credenciais e chaves sempre fora do frontend
legalOrDisclaimerText: Não exibimos integrações sem evidência no produto ou roadmap documentado.
Pagamentos, mensagens e IA dependem de provedores externos e permissões corretas.

cardsOrItems: Google Calendar — status available in data source
WhatsApp Cloud API — requires external configuration
animations: Per-card viewport reveals with up to 300ms staggered transition delay
Card hover lift and cyan border
accessibilityNotes: Integration logos have explicit brand alt text.
Decorative Lucide icons are aria-hidden.
The section has no aria-labelledby/id linkage even though it contains a visible h2 through SectionHeading.
sections.conversionRole: Trust-building and objection handling. Named providers make the platform concrete; caveats reduce the risk of overpromising.
potentialWeaknesses: Internal statusLabel and where fields exist in data but are not rendered, so users cannot visually distinguish available, configuration-required, and in-development integrations except by reading long descriptions.
Infrastructure brands such as Supabase may matter more to technical reviewers than clinic owners.
refactorNotes: Expose a clear visual status badge from existing typed data if product strategy approves; no new data model is needed.

sections.name: Animated Operational Impact Estimates
sections.purpose: Translate centralization into memorable time, task, rework, visibility, and workflow numbers.
sections.targetUserEmotion: Urgency about current waste and optimism about reclaiming time and predictability.
sections.layoutDescription: Left-aligned heading, six large-number cards in 1/2/3 columns, and a full-width small-print estimate disclaimer.
sections.backgroundDescription: Slate-50 with a dark-to-gray animated divider above.

copy.headline: Quanto tempo sua clínica perde hoje fazendo isso manualmente?
copy.subheadline: Cada confirmação por telefone, cada cobrança manual, cada conferência de agenda soma horas que poderiam ser suas. Veja o que a centralização operacional pode representar em números.
bodyTexts: 2.847h/ano economizadas em confirmações, registros e cobranças — Tempo estimado ao digitalizar agendamento, follow-up de pacientes e controle financeiro que hoje consomem horas da recepção e da gestão.
27,4 dias/ano devolvidos para família, pacientes e crescimento — Horas economizadas convertidas em dias que podem voltar para atendimento de qualidade, treinamento ou tempo com quem importa.
183 tarefas/mês manuais que podem sair do seu dia — Confirmações por telefone, anotações avulsas, conciliações de pagamento e conferências de estoque que um fluxo digital assume.
42% menos retrabalho com dados centralizados — Erros, duplicações e retrabalho causados por informações espalhadas em papel, planilhas e mensagens que não se comunicam.
68% mais previsibilidade de gestão — Decisões de equipe, estoque e financeiro tomadas com dados reais em vez de percepção ou relatórios montados manualmente todo mês.
1 fluxo centralizado para toda a operação da clínica — Agenda, pacientes, financeiro, estoque, leads e IA no mesmo ambiente — sem alternar entre sistemas, abas e anotações desconectadas.
legalOrDisclaimerText: Estimativas ilustrativas baseadas em rotinas administrativas comuns de clínicas odontológicas. Resultados podem variar conforme volume de atendimentos, equipe e uso da plataforma.

responsiveBehavior.reducedMotion: Counters immediately show final values and reveal transforms are bypassed.

accessibilityNotes: Section has aria-label Potencial de economia operacional.
Icons are aria-hidden.
Changing numbers are not marked live, avoiding noisy announcements.
The large claims are followed by a visible disclaimer.
sections.conversionRole: Quantified benefit and urgency. It attempts to bridge feature breadth to saved time and management outcomes.
potentialWeaknesses: The exact values are not tied to a visible methodology, customer dataset, baseline clinic size, or calculator; the disclaimer only labels them illustrative.
2,847 hours equals roughly 356 eight-hour workdays, while the adjacent conversion says 27.4 days, making the implied conversion basis unclear and potentially undermining trust.
refactorNotes: A documented calculation model or interactive estimator would make the data defensible; source values are currently static inline constants.

copy.headline: Troque de sistema sem recomeçar do zero

conversionStrategy.firstImpression: Strong category clarity, polished product visual, immediate free-trial offer, and explicit no-card/no-commitment terms. The h1 emphasizes desirability rather than a quantified business outcome.
trustSignals: Real product dashboard in a MacBook
Security language and server-side payment claim
Visible caveats for external providers and NFS-e
Support, legal, privacy, DPO, and cookie links
conversionStrategy.problemAwareness: Six cards accurately capture common fragmented-operation pain, then transition directly into an all-in-one solution.
conversionStrategy.productProof: The hero dashboard is credible and detailed. The later carousel intends to add proof, but inspected assets are promotional creatives rather than the actual screens described, weakening this stage.
conversionStrategy.benefitExplanation: The flow section explains integration conceptually; module cards explain capabilities; impact cards attempt to quantify outcomes. The strongest benefit is reduced retrabalho and centralized control, repeated consistently.
conversionStrategy.pricingClarity: Three plans and exact monthly/annual values are visible, with inclusions and coming-soon states. Annual is default and the recommended Professional plan is easy to identify. The selected plan is not carried into registration.
conversionStrategy.finalCta: Concise and visually distinct, but its hardcoded weekly clinic count creates avoidable credibility risk unless externally verified.
conversionStrategy.audienceAdequacy: The page explains enough breadth for a clinic owner to recognize operational fit and price. It is less specific about implementation timeline, onboarding workload, migration scope, support SLAs, and evidence behind outcome claims.
conversionStrategy.ctaClarity: Primary trial CTA is consistent in hero, pricing, header, and final block. Secondary routes vary appropriately across features, plans, and video. Repetition is high but not inherently confusing because labels remain stable.
abstractOrDistractingAreas: Flow Orbit is visually sophisticated and may distract from the plain six-step value story.
Impact numbers look precise despite being illustrative.
Carousel creatives introduce a different advertising style and do not prove the named product workflows.
Infrastructure-level integration copy may be too technical for some clinic owners.
conversionGaps: No customer testimonial, named clinic, case study, review score, or verifiable adoption proof
No methodology for exact impact estimates
No clearly visible current-vs-roadmap status badge on integration cards
No live product walkthrough beyond a third-party video

technicalImplementation.mainComposition: router indexRoute maps / to a route-lazy LandingPage. LandingPage applies metadata and delayed hash scrolling, wraps content in PublicLayout and LazyMotion(domAnimation), composes 11 content sections, inserts eight SectionDivider transitions, and receives PublicHeader/SiteFooter from PublicLayout.
componentHierarchy: SolutionSection → lazy FlowOrbit → conditional lazy FlowOrbitScene
dataSources: landing-content.ts supplies plan names, prices, savings, and recommendation.
features.ts supplies typed commercial feature availability and plan-card selections.
marketing-pricing.constants.ts supplies plan icons and trust labels.
public-content.ts supplies integration descriptions, benefits, brand assets, sources, locations, and status metadata.
company.ts supplies brand name, slogan, support email, social links, and legal name.
Several section-specific arrays remain inline in component files.
lazyLoadedChunks: SolutionSection lazy-loads FlowOrbit below the fold.
FlowOrbit conditionally lazy-loads FlowOrbitScene only for motion-enabled fine-pointer desktop after intersection.
YouTube iframe is deferred until click but its thumbnail is a remote image.
technicalImplementation.webglAndThree: FlowOrbitScene uses Canvas, useFrame, Drei Html/Line/Sparkles, generated CanvasTexture glow, additive SpriteMaterial, eight sphere nodes, connector lines, HTML labels, rotating group, camera interpolation, and pointer input. DPR is [1,1.8], antialias/alpha enabled, and high-performance requested.
technicalImplementation.gsap: GSAP animates a mutable progress ref from 0 to 1 over 5 seconds infinitely for inward light travelers and scales the module ring from 0.82 to 1 over 1.3 seconds on mount. Both tweens are killed on cleanup.
technicalImplementation.motion: LazyMotion with domAnimation powers Reveal, StaggerGroup, StaggerItem, and MagneticButton. Shared durations and easing live in lib/motion.ts.
technicalImplementation.testingCoverageNotes: Core hero/problem/solution/modules/pricing primitives have focused tests. No dedicated tests were found for the full LandingPage composition, FlowOrbit/FlowOrbitScene, ProductCarouselSection, LandingIntegrationsSection, AnimatedImpactSection, DataMigrationSection, VideoSection, TrialCtaSection, PublicHeader/PublicLayout in the marketing test directory, or landing-specific footer behavior.
buildAndPerformanceNotes: Heavy WebGL dependencies are carefully split from the initial landing route and excluded on mobile/touch/reduced motion.

The audited production build emitted FlowOrbitScene at 982.80 kB minified / 271.45 kB gzip and produced Vite's >500 kB chunk warning; LandingPage itself was 132.60 kB / 41.17 kB gzip and the lightweight FlowOrbit wrapper was 5.66 kB / 2.12 kB gzip.
LazyMotion domAnimation avoids loading the full Motion feature set.
Large raster files remain a major transfer concern and have no srcset/sizes.
The hero image and first below-fold carousel image are eager.
Every scroll event updates PublicLayout state even when boolean thresholds do not change.
Six count-up animations use independent RAF loops but terminate after 2.2 seconds.
The video iframe is deferred until explicit intent.
technicalImplementation.packageManagerAssumption: The repository declares packageManager bun@1.3.9 and all requested quality commands use Bun. No dependency installation is needed or authorized for this documentation task.

possibleIssues.description: The desktop Flow Orbit scene is an unusually large lazy chunk and triggers the production chunk-size warning.
possibleIssues.evidence: The audited bun run build emitted FlowOrbitScene at 982.80 kB minified and 271.45 kB gzip; Vite warned about chunks larger than 500 kB.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Profile whether Three.js, R3F, Drei, and GSAP all materially improve conversion; if retained, investigate narrower imports, dependency chunking, an idle preload after core content, or a lighter canvas/SVG desktop treatment.

possibleIssues.description: Carousel assets do not depict the product screens described by their alt text, captions, and section promise.
possibleIssues.evidence: Direct inspection: carousel.png is a Gestão completa promotional manager creative; carousel1.png promotes access anywhere; carousel2.png promotes scheduling with a staff photo. Source describes agenda week, finance panel, and leads module respectively.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: In a future design/content task, either replace them with real matching product screenshots or rewrite captions and alt text to accurately describe the existing creatives.

possibleIssues.description: Exact operational impact figures appear precise without a visible methodology, and the hours-to-days relationship is unclear.
possibleIssues.evidence: AnimatedImpactSection hardcodes 2,847h/year and 27.4 days/year as adjacent metrics; a general illustrative-results disclaimer is the only source qualification.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Document the assumptions and conversion basis, use a transparent calculator/range, or replace exact values with defensible qualitative benefits.

possibleIssues.description: The final CTA presents a weekly adoption number as live social proof even though it is static and unsourced.
possibleIssues.evidence: TrialCtaSection hardcodes 47 clínicas iniciaram o teste esta semana and wraps it in role=status aria-live=polite; there is no service, prop, date, or update logic.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Connect it to verified data with a freshness policy, or replace it with a non-numeric, verifiable trust statement and remove the live-region semantics.

possibleIssues.description: Landing raster assets are substantially oversized for their rendered roles.
possibleIssues.evidence: MacBook image is 1.21 MB; carousel files are 1.71–1.97 MB; footer logo is 3.56 MB at 3919x3919 rendered 36px; favicon is 4.22 MB at 3919x3919.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Generate correctly sized AVIF/WebP variants, add srcset/sizes, create dedicated favicon/touch-icon sizes, and retain PNG only where alpha/compatibility requires it.

possibleIssues.description: The first carousel image is eagerly loaded despite the carousel appearing after four large content sections.
possibleIssues.evidence: ProductCarouselSection assigns loading=eager to slide index 0; public/carousel.png is approximately 1.87 MB.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Use lazy loading or an intersection-driven preload, and set intrinsic dimensions to preserve layout.

possibleIssues.description: The document language is English while the page is Portuguese.
possibleIssues.evidence: index.html contains html lang=en; all landing copy and metadata are pt-BR Portuguese.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Set the root language to pt-BR in a separate SEO task after confirming all public routes use Portuguese.

possibleIssues.description: Landing metadata is limited to a client-side title and description.
possibleIssues.evidence: usePageMeta only changes document.title and meta[name=description]; no canonical, Open Graph, Twitter, JSON-LD, or initial route-specific metadata was found.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Add route-aware head management or prerendered metadata, including canonical and social cards, when SEO architecture is scheduled.

possibleIssues.evidence: Dots use role=tab/aria-selected, but slides are not tabpanels, dots lack aria-controls, and inactive dots remain in normal tab order.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Either implement the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern fully or use simpler labelled buttons without tab roles.

possibleIssues.description: Desktop dropdowns use menu roles without complete menu keyboard behavior.
possibleIssues.evidence: PublicHeader applies role=menu and role=menuitem; useDropdownNav supports Escape and click-outside but not arrow/Home/End navigation or focus placement.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Implement the complete menu-button keyboard pattern or use disclosure navigation semantics without menu roles.

possibleIssues.description: Selected plan and billing period are lost when the visitor clicks a plan CTA.
possibleIssues.evidence: Every PlanCard links only to /acessar?mode=register regardless of plan.key and billingPeriod.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: If supported by the acquisition flow, encode plan/period in validated search params or persist the selection through a documented registration handoff.

possibleIssues.description: The annual availability caveat may have insufficient contrast.
possibleIssues.evidence: AnnualAvailabilityNote dark variant uses text-slate-600 within a slate-950 pricing section.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Verify WCAG contrast in browser and use a lighter token such as slate-400 if needed.

possibleIssues.description: WhatsApp is presented as an integration and automation benefit while plan rows mark it Em breve.
possibleIssues.evidence: Integration description says infrastructure exists and requires configuration; hero/problem/flow mention confirmations; Professional and Premium feature availability is soon.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Clarify present capability versus planned self-service/plan availability in visible status badges and consistent copy.

possibleIssues.description: No transcript, caption status, or equivalent detailed text alternative is presented for the product video.
possibleIssues.evidence: VideoSection provides iframe title and three summary bullets but no transcript/captions link or duration metadata.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Publish a transcript and confirm captions, then link it adjacent to the play control.

possibleIssues.description: Some continuous Tailwind utility animations and transitions are not explicitly reduced-motion gated.
possibleIssues.evidence: Hero and final CTA use animate-ping/animate-pulse directly; carousel slide transition, header transition, and annual-note transition lack motion-reduce overrides.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Verify Tailwind's generated behavior under reduced motion and add motion-reduce classes where continuous or spatial movement remains.

possibleIssues.description: Fixed header may obscure headings after hash navigation.
possibleIssues.evidence: PublicHeader is fixed; LandingPage and CTA use hash scrolling; #planos and other targets do not show scroll-mt classes.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Add a shared scroll-margin token to public hash-target sections in a future scoped UX fix.

possibleIssues.description: Header scroll tracking causes a React state update for every scroll event.
possibleIssues.evidence: PublicLayout's passive handler directly calls setScrollY(window.scrollY), while rendering only needs two boolean thresholds.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Track threshold state only or use requestAnimationFrame throttling if profiling shows unnecessary render work.

possibleIssues.description: Several conversion-critical landing sections and the full composition lack dedicated tests.
possibleIssues.evidence: No focused landing tests were found for carousel, integrations, impact, migration, video, final CTA, Flow Orbit, or LandingPage composition.
possibleIssues.suggestedFix: Add behavior-focused tests for meaningful interactions and copy/status contracts, avoiding visual class snapshots.

refactorOpportunities.opportunity: Create a typed landing content model for repeated trial terms, trust signals, CTAs, and section copy.
refactorOpportunities.whyItMatters: Hero, pricing, header, and final CTA repeat closely related strings that can drift.
refactorOpportunities.suggestedApproach: Move only stable content into feature data/constants while leaving layout and interaction in components.

refactorOpportunities.opportunity: Share a typed module definition across Flow Orbit, ModulesSection, and possibly navigation.
refactorOpportunities.whyItMatters: The same module concepts are independently named in multiple files, and desktop/fallback orbit data is duplicated.
refactorOpportunities.suggestedApproach: Define stable IDs, labels, icons, and optional routes once, then let each presentation select the fields it needs.

refactorOpportunities.opportunity: Consolidate duplicate poster and module definitions while retaining separate desktop and fallback renderers.
refactorOpportunities.whyItMatters: Reduces drift without coupling WebGL implementation to responsive fallback markup.
refactorOpportunities.suggestedApproach: Extract data and a shared poster component; keep the lazy boundary and static/WebGL components separate.

refactorOpportunities.opportunity: Evaluate a shared LandingSection wrapper and section-header primitive.
refactorOpportunities.whyItMatters: Max-width, px-6/lg:px-8, vertical rhythm, eyebrow, h2, and description patterns recur throughout the page.
refactorOpportunities.suggestedApproach: Extract only after documenting variants for centered/left, dark/light, width, and aria linkage; avoid forcing unique hero/pricing layouts into one abstraction.

refactorOpportunities.opportunity: Introduce a shared marketing CTA group or shared trial-offer model.
refactorOpportunities.whyItMatters: Hero and final CTA use nearly identical primary/secondary patterns and MagneticButton behavior.
refactorOpportunities.suggestedApproach: Share data and wrapper behavior while preserving section-specific button variants and destinations.

refactorOpportunities.opportunity: Consolidate plan prices, feature availability, display labels, and plan-card projections into one typed source.
refactorOpportunities.whyItMatters: Current pricing truth is split across three files, increasing coordination cost and mismatch risk.
refactorOpportunities.suggestedApproach: First define invariants and tests for monthly, annual, availability, and public/admin audiences; migrate incrementally without changing billing logic.

refactorOpportunities.opportunity: Render existing statusLabel and where metadata or simplify unused fields.
refactorOpportunities.whyItMatters: Visible availability is critical to avoiding confusion between live, configuration-required, and roadmap integrations.
refactorOpportunities.suggestedApproach: Add a typed status badge and concise location detail after product/content approval.

refactorOpportunities.opportunity: Create responsive optimized variants and accurate media metadata.
refactorOpportunities.whyItMatters: Current assets dominate likely page transfer and some descriptions do not match visuals.
refactorOpportunities.suggestedApproach: Export WebP/AVIF at measured breakpoints, retain fallbacks, add intrinsic dimensions/srcset/sizes, and validate alt/caption against each file.

refactorOpportunities.opportunity: Standardize reveal transitions now split between Motion components and manual Tailwind class toggles.
refactorOpportunities.whyItMatters: A single motion policy would make timing and reduced-motion compliance easier to audit.
refactorOpportunities.suggestedApproach: Keep WebGL/GSAP specialized, but migrate simple section/card reveals to one helper after visual regression coverage exists.

refactorOpportunities.opportunity: Adopt route-aware initial metadata and structured marketing SEO.
refactorOpportunities.whyItMatters: Client-effect-only title/description omits social/canonical metadata and may weaken crawler previews.
refactorOpportunities.suggestedApproach: Choose a TanStack Router-compatible head/prerender strategy; add pt-BR language, canonical, OG/Twitter, and Organization/SoftwareApplication schema with verified claims.

refactorOpportunities.opportunity: Add a page composition contract and focused tests for conversion interactions.
refactorOpportunities.whyItMatters: Pricing is covered, but carousel, video, final CTA, integration statuses, and responsive orbit selection can regress without targeted checks.
refactorOpportunities.suggestedApproach: Test semantic copy, destinations, state changes, reduced-motion branch, and lazy fallback behavior; do not assert long Tailwind strings.

reviewQuestions: Is the hero's desirability-led promise clearer and more compelling than a direct business-outcome promise for clinic owners?
Does the financial dashboard in the MacBook communicate the breadth named in the hero, or does it over-position DentalFlow as finance-first?
Does Flow Orbit help visitors understand integration, or does its technical spectacle distract from the six-step journey?
Should the carousel use real product screens to fulfill the Na prática promise, or should the section and alt text be reframed around the existing campaign creatives?
Are the six problem cards specific enough to dental operations to differentiate DentalFlow from generic clinic software?
Which of the nine modules should be visually prioritized based on the strongest purchase driver?
Are infrastructure providers such as Supabase meaningful trust signals for clinic owners, or should customer-facing outcomes receive more emphasis?
Are integration availability/configuration/roadmap states clear enough without visible status badges?
Can the exact operational impact figures be defended with a transparent methodology, especially the relationship between 2,847 hours and 27.4 days?
Is the migration promise persuasive enough without scope, timeline, supported-field, and plan-eligibility details?
Is pricing easy to compare on mobile, and are the Starter exclusions and coming-soon items understood without opening the full comparison?
Should the selected plan and billing period persist into registration to reduce conversion friction?
Does the page adequately distinguish currently available WhatsApp capabilities from plan features marked Em breve?
Is the product video accessible and useful without a visible duration, transcript, or caption statement?
Is repeating the free-trial CTA in the fixed header, hero, three pricing cards, and final CTA appropriately persistent or excessive?
Is the hardcoded 47-clinic weekly social-proof claim verifiable and current enough to retain?
Does the playful slogan fit the premium, trustworthy business positioning established elsewhere?
Which section could be removed or simplified with the least loss of conversion information?
Which missing proof element would have the highest impact: customer testimonial, case study, review score, onboarding timeline, or live demo?
Are claims about security, data isolation, AI, migration, and provider availability precise enough for legal and product review?
Does the alternating dark/light rhythm aid scanning, or does it make the long page feel visually complex for a dental clinic owner?
Should the final CTA offer a human-assisted demo/contact path for buyers not ready for self-service registration?
